profile.name: Alisha Chang
tagline: CS Student @ Barnard College, Columbia University
profile.bio: Building full-stack applications with Next.js and Python — most recently a web app for detecting Parkinson’s and tremor symptoms via spiral drawing analysis.

projects.title: Spiral Analysis
projects.description: A non-invasive tool that turns a spiral drawn on a tablet into objective motor measures. Every point (x, y, pressure, time) becomes indices for severity, smoothness, speed, tremor, pressure, and consistency — and with an account each drawing is saved as a baseline, so subtle change surfaces session over session. Built on digitized spiral drawing, an established clinical method for characterizing upper-limb motor performance.

projects.title: Green Infrastructure Data Ingestion
projects.description: Green Infrastructure Data Ingestion is a full-stack web app for registering and managing Green Infrastructure (GI) projects and their datasets. Built with Next.js/React on the frontend and FastAPI/Supabase on the backend, it lets users create and browse projects across four types (Area-Wide, External, Grant, and Onsite), view related datasets (assets, soil borings, permeability tests, and tributary area data), and bulk-import spreadsheet data through an embedded Impler widget. The whole stack — app, API, and the local Impler import platform — runs via Docker Compose.

projects.title: Sylly
projects.description: Sylly is a web application that converts syllabus documents into structured Google Calendar events, helping students plan their semester quickly and efficiently. Users upload syllabi as PDFs, DOCX files, or images, and the app uses Adobe PDF Services for text extraction and Cohere for AI-powered parsing to identify deadlines, exams, and class sessions. Students can review and edit the extracted events before syncing them to Google Calendar via an .ics file. Built with JavaScript, Python, HTML, CSS, and PHP.

projects.title: Redstone Door Tutor
projects.description: Redstone Door Tutor is a Minecraft-themed learning platform built to boost student engagement in Fundamentals of Computer Systems, a notoriously difficult required course. The Flask app walks students through a short guided lesson on building a 2-input redstone door, then checks understanding with an interactive quiz and score. Lesson and quiz content live in a data.json file rather than hard-coded HTML, so pages stay easy to edit and extend. Shaped by user interviews with 12 students across iterations to prioritize interactivity and simplify Minecraft-specific mechanics for non-players.

about.paragraph: I work at the seam between healthcare and software — the Spiral Analysis project came out of wanting objective, repeatable motor measures from something as ordinary as drawing a spiral on a tablet. Most of what I build is full-stack: a Python or C core doing the real work, a JavaScript front end on top.
